correctness.rationale: The published definitions are reconstructed directly. The closure routine checks that each output is an R- or E-palindrome, has the required prefix, and admits no shorter pseudopalindromic prefix-extension. The resulting fifth prefix is exactly the stated 36-bit palindrome. A seven-factor hitting certificate proves a lower bound of five by three disjoint coordinate ranges requiring 2, 1, and 2 selected positions. The explicit five-position set is checked against every occurrence of all 500 distinct nonempty factors. An independent exhaustive pass over all 58,905 four-position subsets confirms the same finite lower bound. The claim is only this finite counterexample, so no finite experiment is extrapolated to an infinite family.

value.rationale: The finding resolves an explicit published conjecture negatively with a small, self-contained witness. The parameter is not an arbitrary slice: the primary paper identifies arbitrary mixed pseudopalindromic closures as the next open class and conjectures the universal bound four. A size-five prefix is therefore a decisive boundary example, and the seven-factor certificate exposes why mixed closures can require an additional attractor position.
